response:
feat(CC-0115): default well-known database/cache/secret fields

- Add defaulting-webhook logic so a minimal managed-mode ControlPlane
  can omit spec.infrastructure and the spec.korc.adminCredential body;
  the webhook materializes the well-known references before validation
- Default the mode-neutral leaves in both managed and brownfield mode:
  database.database to "keystone", database.secretRef.name to
  "keystone-db", and cache.backend to "dogpile.cache.pymemcache"
- Default the managed clusterRef names "openstack-db" and
  "openstack-memcached" only when the brownfield discriminator
  (database.host / cache.servers) is unset, so the database/cache XOR
  validation still holds and an explicit brownfield endpoint is never
  coerced into managed mode
- Default korc.adminCredential.passwordSecretRef.name to
  "keystone-admin", its .key to "password", and
  cloudCredentialsRef.cloudName to "admin"
- Make CloudName optional with a +kubebuilder:default="admin" marker and
  drop it from the CRD required list; the webhook is load-bearing when
  the whole korc block is omitted, since the marker only fires when the
  parent cloudCredentialsRef object is present
- Add Default* constants as the single source of truth; default the
  shared commonv1 leaves (DatabaseSpec, CacheSpec, SecretRefSpec)
  webhook-only with no +kubebuilder:default marker, so a c5c3-specific
  default never leaks into the Keystone CRD that reuses those types
- Regenerate the ControlPlane CRD bases and the Helm chart copy:
  cloudName gains default "admin" and leaves the required list
- Extend the webhook unit tests to assert the eight new defaults on a
  bare ControlPlane, their idempotency, and preservation of explicit
  values
- Add TestDefault_DoesNotInventModeForBrownfield and
  TestDefault_FillsEmptyNameOnPresentClusterRef to cover the brownfield
  guard and the present-but-empty clusterRef name branch
- Add TestIntegration_MinimalManagedToReady, driving the smallest valid
  ControlPlane (only openStackRelease + services.keystone) to aggregate
  Ready=True and asserting the defaults flow through to the projected
  Keystone CR's clusterRefs
- Provision dependencies in driveControlPlaneToAdminCredentialReady at
  the shared Default* names so the helper serves both the multi-CP and
  the minimal-CR integration tests
- Document the optional infrastructure/korc/database/cache/
  passwordSecretRef fields in the CRD reference, the two-layer
  (marker + webhook) vs webhook-only defaulting split, and the
  operational contract that the webhook fills only names/references and
  never invents credential material
- Rewrite the quick-start to show the minimal CR alongside a collapsible
  fully-expanded equivalent, and trim the deploy/kind sample
  ControlPlane to the minimal form
